podcast.title: Dinosaur Species
podcast.body: Mark Knopfler of Dire Straits has a dinosaur named after him, a unique honor that connects the musician to prehistoric life. "Mark Knopfler of Dire Straits has his own dinosaur, which is kind of cool."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Signature Clean Sound
podcast.body: Mark Knopfler is noted for his specific clean, distortion-free sound, which he achieves with the Fender Twin Reverb amplifier. This characteristic sound is particularly evident in his work with Dire Straits. "Think about how Mark Knothler sounds with dire straits."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: TV Commercial for CD Technology
podcast.body: Mark Knopfler, the leader of Dire Straits, appeared in a television commercial to promote the virtues of the compact disc format, aligning with Philips' sponsorship of the band's "Brothers in Arms" tour. "Leader Mark Knopfler even did a TV commercial, extolling the virtues of the CD."

xref.title: Philips Sponsorship and Mark Knopfler Commercial
xref.body: Philips, one of the developers of the compact disc, sponsored Dire Straits' tour for their digitally recorded album "Brothers in Arms." The band's leader, Mark Knopfler, also appeared in a TV commercial to promote the advantages of the CD format, contributing to the album becoming the first to sell a million copies on CD. "Phillips went so far as to sponsor DireStraight's Tour in support of their digitally recorded album Brothers and Arms. Leader Mark Knopfler even did a TV commercial, extolling the virtues of the CD."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Unique Guitar Playing Style
xref.body: Ian, the band's guitarist, developed a unique, self-taught playing style that combines rhythm and lead parts due to being the sole guitarist. He achieves this by playing in drop D tuning, which allows him to play bar chords with one finger while doing leads with the others, describing it as "almost like piano playing." He was influenced by clean players like Andy Summers and Mark Knopfler, as well as Tom Morello and Kim Thayil, and consciously avoided traditional playing. His style is considered "the most unique in the world." "I ended up trying to do both when I became the sole guitar player in this band. And by doing that, I found like dropping to D, I could play, I could play bar chords with one finger and then do a bunch of leads with the other."
